planting.note: Direct sow after the soil has warmed, or start indoors a couple weeks before last frost; Moldavian dragonhead self-seeds readily once established, so expect volunteers in following years.

directions: Direct sow in full sun in average, well-drained soil once the soil has warmed; Moldavian dragonhead is a hardy annual with lemon-mint scented leaves and flowers, both of which are edible and used in teas and as a culinary flavoring. It is an exceptional bee and honey plant, drawing pollinators heavily to its spikes of small blue-violet flowers from midsummer into fall. Grown as a summer annual in nearly every climate, it self-seeds readily in congenial conditions, so deadhead some flower spikes if volunteer seedlings aren't wanted the following year.

planting.note: Direct sow in spring or fall into well-drained, calcareous soil in full sun; burnet saxifrage is slow to establish from seed but low-maintenance once settled.

directions: Direct sow into well-drained, calcareous soil in full sun; burnet saxifrage is a European perennial herb in the carrot family with aromatic, peppery, aniseed-flavored leaves and root, unrelated to the already-present salad burnet (Sanguisorba minor) despite the shared common name. It has a long history as a digestive-bitter ingredient in European herbal liqueurs and was traditionally used as an expectorant for coughs. Once established it needs little attention and tolerates lean, dry soil better than richer garden ground.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun with light afternoon shade in hot climates; prune after flowering to keep growth dense and compact.

directions: Plant in full sun with some afternoon shade in hot climates, in well-drained soil; round-leaf mint bush is an evergreen Australian shrub with intensely mint-eucalyptus scented gray-green leaves, traditionally dried and ground as a bush-food seasoning and brewed as an herbal tea. Showy purple flowers in spring draw bees and other pollinators heavily. It is frost-tender, so treat it as a container plant to overwinter indoors outside zones 9-11, and prune after flowering to maintain a dense, tidy shape.

planting.note: Direct sow in fall or early spring into moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade; wood sanicle naturalizes slowly as a low woodland-floor groundcover.

directions: Direct sow or plant divisions into moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade; wood sanicle is a low-growing European woodland perennial long used as a wound herb, with leaves or a decoction traditionally applied as an astringent for cuts and used as a gargle for sore throat, reflected in the old apothecary proverb 'he that hath sanicle needs no surgeon.' It spreads slowly to form a modest groundcover under trees, with small greenish-white flower clusters in late spring that are easy to overlook. Give it steady moisture and leaf-litter-rich soil similar to its native forest floor habitat.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into consistently moist soil in part shade; small-flowered willowherb spreads somewhat in congenial wet-margin conditions, so site it where that's welcome.

directions: Plant in part shade in consistently moist soil, the wetland-margin conditions this European perennial favors in the wild. Small-flowered willowherb carries small pale-pink flowers through summer and is widely used in German phytotherapy, sold commercially as a tea or tincture for urinary tract and benign prostate support. It spreads somewhat by self-seeding and rhizome in congenial damp sites, making it best suited to a moist shaded border, rain garden margin, or pond edge rather than a tightly controlled bed. Established plantings need little care beyond occasional division to keep the clump in bounds.
